narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Block Signage"**

The building's problems read like the painted signs on a Chicago block: storefront and sign-painter lettering in big block words, flat enamel colour on a cool white wall, and one yellow sign that tells a resident what they can do next. A resident on a phone, often reading in a second language, should see their building's name in block capitals, read the one yellow sign, tap it, and leave.

Density is calm and columnar. Problems are rows, not cards: an issue-colour bar on the left, a block-letter title, plain-language facts, and a day count painted big on the right. Sections are separated by 2px black rules painted across the wall, never boxed. Night mode is the same signs painted on a dark board, not a different theme.

The world refuses the dark SaaS card grid and the cream-paper "ledger" look it replaced. Nothing glows, floats, or shines: no gradients, no glass, no offset shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Big Shoulders block gothic in caps for headings, labels, buttons, and numerals; the phone's own sans for every sentence.
Chrome yellow appears once per screen, on the one unlocked next step.
One flat enamel hue per issue type, the same on every screen.
2px black rules instead of card boxes; corners of 2 to 6px.
One motion moment: the "Me too" count bump.

rules.name: The One Yellow Sign Rule
rules.body: Chrome yellow marks the one next step a resident can take now. It is never decoration, never a highlight, and never a warning. The single other use is the "Me too" count flash, which confirms the resident's own action and fades within 1.4s.

rules.name: The Neutral Warning Rule
rules.body: Warnings use the Wall Shade board with a black rule and black text. Yellow belongs to the next step only.

rules.name: The One Hue Per Problem Rule
rules.body: An issue type's enamel is the same on every screen and in every mode's lightness step. Never pick an issue colour per page, and never give two issue types the same hue except the slate pair.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders sets h1 to h4, labels, buttons, and numerals, always in caps. It never sets a sentence. Anything a resident reads as a sentence, in any language, is the system font.

rules.name: The Lined-Up Numbers Rule
rules.body: Dates, counts, and table cells use tabular figures so they line up in columns.

rules.name: The Flat Paint Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest never have a shadow. No gradients, no glass, no backdrop blur, no hard offset shadows.

rules.name: The Rule Not Box Rule
rules.body: Group content under a 2px black top rule. Do not draw a four-sided card around it.

dos: **Do** give each screen at most one Chrome Sign Yellow board, and only for a step the resident can take now.
**Do** key every issue colour through `data-issue` so the hue matches across rows, filters, tiles, and plates.
**Do** set h1 to h4, labels, buttons, and numerals in Big Shoulders caps; set every sentence in the system font.
**Do** separate sections with a 2px Enamel Black rule and divide list items with 1px light rules.
**Do** keep corners between 2px and 6px and touch targets at least 48px (40px for compact buttons and tags).
**Do** paint the same signs on Night Board in dark mode, using the lighter enamel steps from `base.css`.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion` and keep print output black on white with the rules intact.
donts: **Don't** use yellow for warnings, highlights, badges, or decoration; warnings are a Wall Shade board with a black rule.
**Don't** wrap content in four-sided cards or add resting shadows.
**Don't** use gradients, glass, backdrop blur, or hard offset shadows.
**Don't** set body sentences in Big Shoulders; it does not cover the languages the notices use.
**Don't** add motion beyond the "Me too" count bump and short colour transitions.
**Don't** introduce a new issue hue without adding it to the enamel set in `base.css` for both light and dark.
